One of the biggest mistakes I made early in trading was believing that if I wasn’t taking trades, I wasn’t improving.

So I would open my charts every day looking for something.

Monday? Trade.

Tuesday? Trade.

Wednesday? Definitely trade.

Even when the market wasn’t giving me anything clear, I would somehow convince myself that a setup was there.

And that was the problem.

I wasn’t reading the market anymore.

I was trying to make the market fit what I wanted to see.

It took me a while to understand that professional trading is almost quite the opposite.

Some days, the best analysis ends with:

“There is nothing here for me.”

Some weeks, price may accumulate longer than expected.

Sometimes your weekly DOL is clear, but the entry model never forms.

Sometimes price reaches your POI and gives absolutely no confirmation.

You don’t have to participate in every move.

The real skill is knowing the difference between:

A market you don’t understand

and

A market that hasn’t given you an entry yet.

Both require patience.

Your edge does not need to appear every day for it to be profitable.

In fact, if you constantly need a trade every single day…

You probably don’t have an edge.

You have an addiction to activity.
